text: What does a router do with a packet after forwarding it?
choices: Forgets it entirely — forwarding is stateless with respect to conversations
Caches it in case of retransmission
explanation: Statelessness is what allows a router to handle millions of simultaneous flows in hardware with no per-flow memory, and to reboot without disrupting conversations. It is the direct operational payoff of the end-to-end argument.
